intuition.title: Study context: Precursor chemistry and distinct synthesis controls
intuition.text: Aminoarsine is conditioned with oleylamine at 40 °C until bubbling stops, consistent with source-proposed transamination. Exact reacted molecular species is unknown. The quantified 1 mmol cyanoborohydride recipe gives pure InAs; the 0.5 mmol and 3/6 mmol comparisons are distinct incompletely specified observations. Excess reductant promotes metallic In, while NaCl is a washing-dependent by-product.
intuition.source_locator: Supporting Information PDF p. 3,13, Sections 1.2.1–1.2.2, 2.1 and Figure S2

intuition.title: Study context: Washing comparison does not overwrite the reported recipe
intuition.text: The typical recipe explicitly uses a first toluene/methanol/isopropanol wash and two later toluene/ethanol washes, each centrifuged at 4500 rpm for 10 min. Figure S2b compares ethanol versus methanol purification and reports NaCl removal using methanol. Complete alternative volumes and sequence are not supplied, so the observation is preserved separately.
intuition.source_locator: Supporting Information PDF p. 4,13, Workup and Figure S2b

intuition.title: Study context: Parent QDs and ligand-exchanged QDs are separate samples
intuition.text: Pristine oleylamine-capped InAs has a reported 2.2 nm TEM mean and In/As ratio 1.04. After exchange, the source reports retained phase, morphology and absorption, decreased interparticle distance, loss of N 1s, S 2p near 163 eV and In/As 1.13. It does not report a newly measured 2.2 nm mean for the exchanged sample.
intuition.source_locator: Supporting Information PDF p. 14–15,26–27, Figures S3 and S12

intuition.title: Study context: Surface chemistry is not bulk phase purity
intuition.text: Pristine XRD is consistent with zinc-blende InAs, while XPS shows about 3 at% surface oxygen and a weak As(III)-consistent contribution. A phase-pure diffraction pattern does not establish an oxygen-free surface. The ICSD patterns are references, not refined specimen atomic coordinates.
intuition.source_locator: Supporting Information PDF p. 14–15, Section 2.2 and Figure S3

intuition.title: Study context: Electrode fabrication and flooding are source-specific contexts
intuition.text: Native oleylamine-capped QDs are deposited from toluene with a later Nafion layer for H-cell tests. Exchanged QDs are deposited from ethanol with a mixed binder ink for flow-cell tests. Source observations associate residual oleylamine with loss of support hydrophobicity; the mechanism is proposed, and no contact angle is measured or inferred from the droplet photograph.
intuition.source_locator: Supporting Information PDF p. 5–6,25–26, Electrode crafting and Figure S11

intuition.title: Study context: Catalytic metrics belong to the electrode and testing regime
intuition.text: Near-unity formate Faradaic efficiency is the flow-cell result for exchanged-QD electrodes in 1 M KOH. The native-ligand H-cell in 1 M KHCO3 peaks near 55% at −5 mA/cm2. These are not properties of an isolated pristine particle or claims of complete electrochemical parameter coverage. Main-figure captions retain one-hour chronopotentiometry and their controls.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Figures 1–3 and catalytic discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Reconstruction and active phase are distinct kinds of evidence
intuition.text: Post-electrolysis STEM/EDS indicates In-rich agglomerates and partially oxidized InAs1−x; ex-situ XPS is In-rich and As-depleted with predominantly In2O3. Metallic indium as the operative active phase is the authors’ interpretation of electrochemistry, not the same claim as the ex-situ oxide signal. Detailed SI post-electrolysis specimen comparisons are outside the selected pages.

bindings.caption: Prepare the amino-As/oleylamine solution in an N2 glovebox and heat until bubbling ceases. The source associates bubbling with transamination; no duration or isolated transaminated formula is assigned. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Stir InCl3 with oleylamine and octadecene in a glovebox. The sentence does not state a distinct gas identity for this indium-conditioning step. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Vacuum dry an empty 25 mL flask at room temperature on a standard Schlenk line. This step is parallel to precursor preparation; vacuum pressure is unknown. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.
Switch the Schlenk line to Ar and inject the indium solution into the dried flask. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Raise the solution to the source injection temperature. Ramp rate and dwell before injection are not given. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Disperse 1 mmol sodium cyanoborohydride in 0.5 mL oleylamine; no temperature or conditioning time is stated. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Inject the conditioned arsenic precursor together with the reducing-agent dispersion into the hot indium solution. No rate is supplied. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

React for 1 h following the 240 °C injection; the described reaction temperature is retained without inventing a separate temperature program. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Cool to room temperature and transfer into the glovebox. Numerical room temperature and cooling duration are absent. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Wash with toluene, methanol and isopropanol; mixing proportions and volumes are absent. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.
Centrifuge and discard the supernatant, retaining the precipitate. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Perform two additional washes with toluene and ethanol. Each cycle is followed by 4500 rpm centrifugation for 10 min and supernatant disposal. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

Disperse the final precipitate in toluene for characterization and electrochemical testing. Dispersion volume and concentration are unspecified. Original conceptual scene; no unreported apparatus dimensions, heating device or measured particle geometry implied.

general_background.title: Injection and precursor supply
general_background.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
